book.title: Biology: A Global Approach
book.authors: Neil A. Campbell, Lisa A. Urry, Michael L. Cain, Steven A. Wasserman, Peter V. Minorsky, Jane B. Reece
book.fullBookDescription: Complete Part 1 PDF containing introductory chapters through Unit 3 (Chapters 1-17), including all diagrams, inquiry figures, and scientific exercises.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Core themes and scientific inquiry in modern biology

units.title: Biology and Its Themes
units.summary: Explores the overarching themes of biology, the hierarchy of biological organization, evolutionary mechanisms, and the scientific inquiry process.
concepts: 1.1 The study of life reveals unifying themes
1.2 The Core Theme: Evolution accounts for the unity and diversity of life
1.3 In studying nature, scientists make observations and form and test hypotheses
1.4 Science benefits from a cooperative approach and diverse viewpoints

sections.title: Unit 1: The Role of Chemistry in Biology
sections.description: Chemical basis of life, atoms, water, carbon diversity, biological macromolecules, and energy transformation

units.title: Atoms and Molecules
units.summary: Matter, elements, isotopes, atomic structure, electron configurations, and chemical bonding (covalent, ionic, hydrogen bonds).
concepts: 2.1 Matter consists of chemical elements in pure form and in combinations called compounds
2.2 An element's properties depend on the structure of its atoms
2.3 The formation and function of molecules depend on chemical bonding
2.4 Chemical reactions make and break chemical bonds

units.title: The Chemistry of Water
units.summary: Polarity of water, hydrogen bonding, emergent properties sustaining life, temperature moderation, and acids/bases/pH scale.
concepts: 3.1 Polar covalent bonds in water molecules result in hydrogen bonding
3.2 Four emergent properties of water contribute to Earth's suitability for life
3.3 Acidic and basic conditions affect living organisms

units.title: Carbon: The Basis of Molecular Diversity
units.summary: Carbon skeleton architectures, hydrocarbons, isomers (structural, cis-trans, enantiomers), and characteristic functional groups.
concepts: 4.1 Organic chemistry is the study of carbon compounds
4.2 Carbon atoms can form diverse molecules by bonding to four other atoms
4.3 A few chemical groups are key to molecular function

units.title: Biological Macromolecules and Lipids
units.summary: Structure, synthesis, and breakdown of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins (primary through quaternary structures), and nucleic acids (DNA/RNA).
concepts: 5.1 Macromolecules are polymers, built from monomers
5.2 Carbohydrates serve as fuel and building material
5.3 Lipids are a diverse group of hydrophobic molecules
5.4 Proteins include a diversity of structures, resulting in a wide range of functions
5.5 Nucleic acids store, transmit, and help express hereditary information
5.6 Genomics and proteomics have transformed biological inquiry

units.title: Energy and Life
units.summary: Metabolism, laws of thermodynamics, free energy changes (delta G), ATP structure and phosphorylation, enzyme kinetics, and allosteric regulation.
concepts: 6.1 An organism's metabolism transforms matter and energy, subject to laws of thermodynamics
6.2 Free-energy change tells whether a reaction occurs spontaneously
6.3 ATP powers cellular work by coupling exergonic to endergonic reactions
6.4 Enzymes speed up metabolic reactions by lowering energy barriers
6.5 Regulation of enzyme activity helps control metabolism

sections.title: Unit 2: Cell Biology
sections.description: Structure and function of prokaryotic & eukaryotic cells, membranes, cell communication, energy conversion, and division

units.title: Cell Structure and Function
units.summary: Microscopy, organelle structures, endomembrane system, nucleus, ribosomes, mitochondria, chloroplasts, cytoskeleton, and extracellular matrices.
concepts: 7.1 Biologists use microscopes and biochemistry to study cells
7.2 Eukaryotic cells have internal membranes that compartmentalize their functions
7.3 The eukaryotic cell's genetic instructions are housed in the nucleus and carried out by ribosomes
7.4 The endomembrane system regulates protein traffic and performs metabolic functions
7.5 Mitochondria and chloroplasts change energy from one form to another
7.6 The cytoskeleton coordinates cellular movement and structure
7.7 Extracellular components and cellular junctions coordinate cell activities

units.title: Cell Membranes
units.summary: Fluid mosaic model, membrane fluidity, transport proteins, passive transport (diffusion & osmosis), active transport (pumps & cotransport), and bulk transport.
concepts: 8.1 Cellular membranes are fluid mosaics of lipids and proteins
8.2 Membrane structure results in selective permeability
8.3 Passive transport is diffusion of a substance across a membrane with no energy investment
8.4 Active transport uses energy to move solutes against their gradients
8.5 Bulk transport across the plasma membrane occurs by exocytosis and endocytosis

units.title: Cellular Signaling
units.summary: Signal transduction paradigms: reception (GPCRs, RTKs, ion channels), intracellular cascades (phosphorylation, cAMP, Ca2+), cellular responses, and apoptosis.
concepts: 9.1 External signals are converted to responses within the cell
9.2 Reception: A signaling molecule binds to a receptor protein, causing shape change
9.3 Transduction: Cascades of molecular interactions relay signals from receptors to target molecules
9.4 Response: Cell signaling leads to regulation of transcription or cytoplasmic activities
9.5 Apoptosis integrates multiple cell-signaling pathways

units.title: Cell Respiration
units.summary: Catabolic pathways, redox reactions, glycolysis, pyruvate oxidation, citric acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation (ETC and chemiosmosis), and fermentation.
concepts: 10.1 Catabolic pathways yield energy by oxidizing organic fuels
10.2 Glycolysis harvests chemical energy by oxidizing glucose to pyruvate
10.3 After pyruvate is oxidized, citric acid cycle completes energy-yielding oxidation
10.4 During oxidative phosphorylation, chemiosmosis couples electron transport to ATP synthesis
10.5 Fermentation and anaerobic respiration enable cells to produce ATP without oxygen
10.6 Glycolysis and the citric acid cycle connect to many other metabolic pathways

units.title: Photosynthetic Processes
units.summary: Chloroplast ultrastructure, electromagnetic spectrum, chlorophylls, light reactions (photosystems II & I, photophosphorylation), Calvin cycle, and C3/C4/CAM adaptations.
concepts: 11.1 Photosynthesis converts light energy to chemical energy of food
11.2 The light reactions convert solar energy to chemical energy of ATP and NADPH
11.3 The Calvin cycle uses chemical energy of ATP and NADPH to reduce CO2 to sugar
11.4 Alternative mechanisms of carbon fixation have evolved in hot, arid climates

units.title: Mitosis
units.summary: Cell cycle phases (G1, S, G2, M), mitotic apparatus and chromosome distribution, cytokinesis, cell cycle checkpoints (cyclins & CDKs), and cancer loss of control.
concepts: 12.1 Most cell division results in genetically identical daughter cells
12.2 The mitotic phase alternates with interphase in the cell cycle
12.3 The eukaryotic cell cycle is regulated by a molecular control system

sections.title: Unit 3: The Genetic Basis of Life
sections.description: Meiosis, Mendelian genetics, chromosomal inheritance, DNA replication, gene expression, and modern biotechnology

units.title: Sexual Life Cycles and Meiosis
units.summary: Heredity, homologous chromosomes, meiosis I and II stages, crossing over, and origins of genetic variation among offspring.
concepts: 13.1 Offspring acquire genes from parents by inheriting chromosomes
13.2 Fertilization and meiosis alternate in sexual life cycles
13.3 Meiosis reduces the number of chromosome sets from diploid to haploid
13.4 Genetic variation produced in sexual life cycles contributes to evolution

units.title: Mendelian Genetics
units.summary: Mendel's experimental model, law of segregation, law of independent assortment, Punnett squares, dominance relationships, multiple alleles, pleiotropy, epistasis, and human pedigrees.
concepts: 14.1 Mendel used the scientific approach to identify two laws of inheritance
14.2 Probability laws govern Mendelian inheritance
14.3 Inheritance patterns are often more complex than predicted by simple Mendelian genetics
14.4 Many human traits follow Mendelian patterns of inheritance

units.title: Linkage and Chromosomes
units.summary: Chromosomal theory of inheritance, sex-linked genes, X inactivation (Barr bodies), linked genes, recombination frequencies, genetic maps, chromosomal aberrations (aneuploidy, polyploidy), and genomic imprinting.
concepts: 15.1 Mendelian inheritance has its physical basis in the behavior of chromosomes
15.2 Sex-linked genes exhibit unique patterns of inheritance
15.3 Linked genes tend to be inherited together because they are located near each other on the same chromosome
15.4 Alterations of chromosome number or structure cause some genetic disorders
15.5 Some inheritance patterns are exceptions to standard chromosome theory

units.title: Nucleic Acids and Inheritance
units.summary: Identification of DNA as the genetic material (Griffith, Hershey-Chase), Watson-Crick double helix, semiconservative replication mechanism, DNA polymerases, replication fork enzymes, and proofreading/repair.
concepts: 16.1 DNA is the genetic material
16.2 Many proteins work together in DNA replication and repair
16.3 A chromosome consists of a DNA molecule packed together with proteins

units.title: Expression of Genes
units.summary: Central dogma (DNA -> RNA -> Protein), genetic code and codons, transcription (promoters, RNA polymerase, elongation), post-transcriptional processing (5' cap, poly-A tail, RNA splicing), translation (tRNA, ribosomes, polypeptide elongation), and mutations.
concepts: 17.1 Genes specify proteins via transcription and translation
17.2 Transcription is the DNA-directed synthesis of RNA
17.3 Eukaryotic cells modify RNA after transcription
17.4 Translation is the RNA-directed synthesis of a polypeptide
17.5 Mutations of one or a few nucleotides can affect protein structure and function

sections.title: Future Units (Part 2 - Coming Soon)
sections.description: Chapters 18 through 56 covering Gene Expression Control, Biotechnology, Evolution, Diversity, Plant & Animal Biology, and Ecology.

units.title: Control of Gene Expression
units.summary: Operons in bacteria, eukaryotic chromatin remodeling, transcription factors, noncoding RNAs, and cancer genetics.

units.title: DNA Technology
units.summary: Gene cloning, PCR, DNA sequencing, CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, and forensic applications.

units.title: The Evolution of Genomes
units.summary: Comparative genomics, noncoding DNA, multigene families, and duplication in genome evolution.

units.title: Unit 4: Evolution (Chapters 21-25)
units.summary: Darwinian evolution, phylogenetics, population genetics, Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, speciation, and macroevolution.

units.title: Unit 5: The Diversity of Life (Chapters 26-34)
units.summary: Viruses, prokaryotes, protists, origin of land plants, fungi, and the radiation of invertebrate and vertebrate animals.

units.title: Unit 6: Plant Form and Function (Chapters 35-39)
units.summary: Plant anatomy, xylem and phloem transport, mineral nutrition, angiosperm reproduction, and plant hormones.

units.title: Unit 7: Animal Form and Function (Chapters 40-50)
units.summary: Homeostasis, nutrition, cardiovascular systems, immunology, osmoregulation, endocrinology, reproduction, neurobiology, and sensory physiology.

units.title: Unit 8: The Ecology of Life (Chapters 51-56)
units.summary: Biosphere ecology, behavioral ecology, population dynamics, community interactions, biogeochemical cycles, and global conservation.
